column1: # name-create.tsv (harbor#978) — core's own create commands whose new name context-rules/user/name-note-create.sh judges at birth.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The injector ships with no rows (it reads <config dir>/name-create.d/*.tsv), and a pack's rows land
# there as name-create.d/<repo-id>.tsv (bin/pack.sh). Nothing shipped a row, so the injector never fired on any box. These
# are the rows for the commands that birth a credential's name: bin/secret, harbor access add, and a gcloud service
# account's display name. bin/context-injection-install.sh installs this file as name-create.d/harbor.tsv beside the
# injector, and `harbor check --live` (check context.name-create) is red when that folder holds no row.
# FORMAT  <ERE matched against the command, ending where the name begins> TAB <surface> TAB <note>
#   The first word after the match that is not a flag is the name, or the whole of a quoted one. The surface is a
#   surfaces.tsv id that --check accepts (checked = tree or check). # lines are comments.

column3: A secret ref is <system>-<service>-<identity>-<purpose> (harbor/D-36); register it first: harbor access add.
harbor access add refuses this ref; the fix line it prints is the compliant name.
Rename the object on the vendor first, so its console says whose it is.
The display name is what the Cloud console shows for this service account.
